newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo stocks seen moving little on lack of sellers.
newsitem.headline: Colombo stocks seen moving little on lack of sellers.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks, which rose sharply in the past two weeks, are seen moving little on Wednesday mostly on lack of liquidity even as buying pressure continues, brokers said.
They said retail sellers were in the market and foreign buying was expected, but added that large quantities of shares were not available.
"Main funds are there to buy, but it is difficult to find quantities. The index should not move too much," said Shanil Perera of Lanka Securities.
Sri Lanka stocks closed slightly higher on Tuesday when the all share index rose 2.8 points to close at 774.6, mainly due to the sale of a large block of shares of a blue chip finance firm.

"There is foreign purchase seen. Also, there is a bit of profit-taking by retailers amidst buying pressure. All this should see the market momentum carrying on," said a broker with CT Smith Stock Brokers.
Brokers said the index rose more than 40 points in the past two weeks after analysts upgraded corporate earnings forecast for 1997 and 1998.
